text:
emily: customer reports streaming chat responses stalling in prod edge (Vercel). Node TS SDK ReadableStream never yields chunks after first few, client waits forever. says sometimes get HTTP 415 earlier in same session. tickets: #INC-3542 :thinking:

kai: can you paste minimal repro and response headers? 415 usually content-type mismatch. also which sdk + node version? :eyes:

emily: sdk @redwood/js v0.7.1, node 18.14, edge runtime on vercel. repro steps they gave: 1) call /v1/chat/stream with streaming param, 2) client uses fetch + getReader on response.body. sometimes works, sometimes nothing. attached logs show one session with 415 then subsequent streams hang.

sam: do we have any edge middleware that rewrites headers? last time similar behaviour was an internal proxy adding `content-encoding: gzip` which broke streaming semantics in some edge runtimes.

jess: quick ask — how are they consuming the stream? typical pattern: 
```
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  // process chunk
}
```
If the response comes back with `Content-Type: application/json` rather than `text/event-stream` or `application/octet-stream` some clients treat it differently.

emily: pasted headers from their failing run: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `content-encoding: gzip`, `transfer-encoding: chunked`. When it 415'd earlier: `content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

kai: interesting — 415 earlier suggests upstream rejected the request (maybe content-type on request was wrong). The `text/plain + gzip` combo can be problematic for streaming in Vercel edge + Node fetch polyfills. Can we reproduce locally with `vercel dev`?

emily: created minimal repro repo and ran on vercel dev — saw the hang intermittently. repro link: https://github.com/redwood/repro-stream-invalid-content (internal). steps in README.

sam: i'm going to try swapping out compression. if gzip present, the runtime might buffer until full chunk to decompress. suggestion: ensure upstream (our gateway) sets `content-encoding` only when response is complete, or disable gzip for SSE endpoints.

jess: also check SDK version. we patched streaming header handling in v0.8.0 to normalize Content-Type and avoid closing the stream when `text/plain` is returned by some proxies. emily can you ask customer to test with v0.8.2?

emily: asked customer to test with v0.8.2 and to force disable gzip in their CDN. they replied: after upgrading sdk, initial 415 disappeared, streaming still stalls ~1/10 requests. they disabled gzip and the problem went away. :relieved:

kai: ok root cause likely: external CDN/proxy adding gzip + content-type coercion leads to the runtime buffering and not flushing ReadableStream chunks. mitigation: 1) update docs to recommend disabling gzip for streaming endpoints and ensure Content-Type is `text/event-stream` or `application/octet-stream`; 2) SDK: in next release add defensive logic to accept `text/plain` with streaming and avoid treating it as non-streaming; 3) ops: add rule to gateway to skip compression on /v1/*/stream.

sam: i've opened infra ticket INF-812 to disable compression for streaming routes on gateway and to add a health test that fetches a 30s SSE and asserts chunk delivery within 2s intervals.

emily: customer confirmed full fix after gateway change. closing escalation. adding notes to support runbook. thanks everyone :tada:
